gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 21?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 21 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover, widespread showers, and afternoon thunderstorms driven by a moist, unstable air mass are capping solar insolation and limiting daytime heating across Munich on August 21. Official forecasts from multiple sources converge on a maximum of 20–23 °C, well below the long-term average high of ~24 °C, as northeasterly to northwesterly flow advects cooler maritime air and enhances evaporative cooling from heavy precipitation. Small differences among leading market outcomes (21–23 °C) hinge on the precise timing and intensity of convective cells: earlier or more intense rain suppresses the peak by an additional 1–2 °C, while brief breaks in cloud cover could allow marginal warming toward the upper end of the range. Updated model runs and surface observations through the afternoon will be the key catalysts for any late shifts in trader sentiment.

This aligns with National Weather Service model guidance and falls near the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 82.7°F, with no strong warm advection or clear-sky conditions to push readings higher. Trader consensus at 100% for the 84–85°F bin reflects convergence across official preliminary climatological data (CF6 reports) and real-time ASOS measurements. An unlikely upward revision from station-specific microclimates or post-processed quality control could theoretically shift the outcome, though current data alignment makes such changes improbable before market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecasts for Munich on August 22, 2026, center on a maximum of 20–23 °C under broken clouds and scattered showers, producing the tight clustering of market probabilities around 21 °C (36.5 %), 22 °C (27.0 %), and 20 °C (19.5 %).**

Official guidance from the Met Office, BBC, AccuWeather, and timeanddate.com converges on daytime highs near 21–22 °C (roughly 70 °F), with passing showers or thundery activity expected to reduce insolation and cap afternoon warming. Recent model runs highlight a transient Atlantic front or upper-level trough increasing cloud cover and precipitation chances, which historically suppresses peak temperatures by 2–4 °C relative to clear-sky climatology for late August (long-term average highs near 22–23 °C). 

Wind direction (southwesterly to westerly, 7–10 mph) and surface moisture from overnight lows in the low teens °C further limit boundary-layer heating. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probabilities to the narrow 20–22 °C band, reflecting both the consensus forecast and residual uncertainty over exact shower timing and any late-day clearing that could allow a brief spike toward 23 °C. Updated NWP guidance and radar trends through the evening of August 21 will be the key near-term catalysts.

**Persistent northeasterly flow and widespread cloud cover plus showers are suppressing daytime heating in New York City, driving trader consensus toward a highest temperature (typically measured at Central Park) in the mid-to-upper 70s on August 22.** 

National Weather Service and private forecasts issued August 20–21 consistently call for mostly cloudy skies, a 60% chance of showers (with isolated thunderstorms possible), and highs near 74–76°F under humid conditions with northeast winds of 5–10 mph. This setup follows recent cooler readings (e.g., highs in the low-to-mid 70s on August 20) and contrasts with the long-term average high of ~82–83°F for the date. 

The leading market buckets (76–77°F at 44.5%, 78–79°F at 21.5%, 74–75°F at 17.5%) closely track these official guidance products, with lower-probability tails reflecting residual uncertainty in exact convective timing and cloud breaks that could allow brief additional warming. New model runs and morning observations on August 22 will provide the final inputs for resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Cloud cover and scattered showers expected on August 22 are the main near-term factors moderating Tokyo’s peak temperature, keeping market-implied probabilities concentrated on 30–32 °C.** Official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance issued August 21 forecasts a cloudy day with occasional showers later, maximum around 33 °C and minimum 24 °C, while other models center closer to 31 °C. These conditions reduce solar heating compared with clear-sky scenarios that would otherwise push readings higher under the season’s dominant Pacific High. 

August climatology for Tokyo shows a normal daily maximum near 30.8 °C, but 2026 has featured above-average warmth across Japan due to a strengthened subtropical ridge. The combination of lingering summer heat with increased moisture and reduced insolation from clouds therefore anchors trader consensus around the 31 °C outcome (36 % implied) and 32 °C (25.5 %), with lower probabilities assigned to 33 °C or above given the precipitation risk. Updated JMA or numerical model runs on the morning of the 22nd will be the next key data point for any late shifts.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent northeasterly flow and widespread cloud cover plus showers are suppressing daytime heating in New York City, driving trader consensus toward a highest temperature (typically measured at Central Park) in the mid-to-upper 70s on August 22.** 

National Weather Service and private forecasts issued August 20–21 consistently call for mostly cloudy skies, a 60% chance of showers (with isolated thunderstorms possible), and highs near 74–76°F under humid conditions with northeast winds of 5–10 mph. This setup follows recent cooler readings (e.g., highs in the low-to-mid 70s on August 20) and contrasts with the long-term average high of ~82–83°F for the date. 

The leading market buckets (76–77°F at 44.5%, 78–79°F at 21.5%, 74–75°F at 17.5%) closely track these official guidance products, with lower-probability tails reflecting residual uncertainty in exact convective timing and cloud breaks that could allow brief additional warming. New model runs and morning observations on August 22 will provide the final inputs for resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent JMA and ensemble forecasts for Tokyo on August 22 indicate a maximum near 32–33°C under mostly cloudy skies with 20–50% afternoon shower chances, explaining the market’s tight clustering around 31–32°C (combined ~67% implied probability). Model spread in rainfall timing and coverage creates the narrow gap between 31°C and 32°C, with any earlier or heavier showers likely to suppress the high further and later clearing supporting the upper end. Updated JMA guidance and hourly observations tomorrow morning will be the key near-term catalyst for shifts in trader positioning.

Typical late-August maxima near 23–25°C are suppressed by these conditions, while model consensus leaves limited room for 24°C or higher (18.5%). Hourly data indicate brief spikes near 23°C possible before rain intensifies, creating the narrow spread traders are pricing. Updated model runs and any late clearing could still shift the exact maximum before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts for Munich on August 23, 2026, center on a daytime high near the long-term August average of 22–23°C under clearing skies and light northerly winds.** Multiple models, including those from WeatherBug, Globalmeteo, Weather Atlas, and MeteoNews, project highs of 21–23°C (roughly 70–73°F) with mostly clear to partly cloudy conditions and minimal precipitation risk after earlier showers.

A surface high building over the region, combined with northerly flow, has stabilized the air mass following August 21 thunderstorms that delivered widespread rain and cooler temperatures. This setup favors efficient daytime solar heating without excessive moisture or strong winds, keeping maxima close to climatological norms (historical averages near 22°C). Ensemble consistency across sources reduces the chance of significant outliers, aligning with the market’s heavy weighting toward 22°C (44%) and 23°C (29.5%).

Lower probabilities for 20°C or below reflect the expected clearing and seasonal insolation, while tails above 24°C remain slim absent any warm advection or subsidence strengthening. Updated model runs and official DWD guidance in the next 24–48 hours will provide the final refinement ahead of resolution.

**Recent forecasts from the Met Office and other sources indicate settled high-pressure conditions developing over the UK this weekend, favoring dry, bright weather with sunny spells for London on August 23.** This setup supports maximum temperatures near or slightly above the seasonal average of roughly 22–23°C, aligning with the market's tight clustering around 23–25°C.

High pressure suppresses cloud formation and precipitation while allowing greater solar insolation during daylight hours, which helps drive daytime peaks higher than under a more unsettled, showery regime. Light winds or calm conditions under the ridge can further enhance surface heating by limiting mixing with cooler air aloft. Conversely, any lingering Atlantic moisture, increased cloud cover, or a slight shift in the high's position could cap the peak at 23°C or below by reducing net radiation.

The closely matched probabilities for 23°C (28%) and 24°C (37.5%), with 25°C at 17%, reflect ensemble model spread in the precise timing and strength of this high-pressure build. Updated runs over the next 24–48 hours, particularly from the Met Office and ECMWF, will likely refine whether the peak reaches the upper or lower end of that narrow range before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecasts from the Met Office and other sources indicate settled high-pressure conditions developing over the UK this weekend, favoring dry, bright weather with sunny spells for London on August 23.** This setup supports maximum temperatures near or slightly above the seasonal average of roughly 22–23°C, aligning with the market's tight clustering around 23–25°C.

High pressure suppresses cloud formation and precipitation while allowing greater solar insolation during daylight hours, which helps drive daytime peaks higher than under a more unsettled, showery regime. Light winds or calm conditions under the ridge can further enhance surface heating by limiting mixing with cooler air aloft. Conversely, any lingering Atlantic moisture, increased cloud cover, or a slight shift in the high's position could cap the peak at 23°C or below by reducing net radiation.

The closely matched probabilities for 23°C (28%) and 24°C (37.5%), with 25°C at 17%, reflect ensemble model spread in the precise timing and strength of this high-pressure build. Updated runs over the next 24–48 hours, particularly from the Met Office and ECMWF, will likely refine whether the peak reaches the upper or lower end of that narrow range before resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 21 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast ensembles from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and German Weather Service favor a Munich peak near 22°C on August 21, driven by post-heatwave cooling that has lowered daytime maxima after earlier August warmth. Climatological averages place typical highs at 23–24°C, yet current atmospheric conditions, including shifting steering patterns and reduced insolation, support the market’s heavy weighting on 22°C (74.5% implied probability) over 23°C (20.5%). Model spread remains modest but acknowledges residual uncertainty from possible afternoon clearing or localized advection that could push readings into the 24°C+ bin. Official verification will rely on Munich’s primary meteorological station measurements.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from sources including the Deutscher Wetterdienst-influenced models and international ensembles project a high of 20–21°C for Munich on August 22 under partly cloudy skies, westerly winds of 10–12 mph, and low precipitation odds around 20–25%. A frontal passage and associated showers on August 21 have advected cooler, more stable air masses northward, suppressing daytime heating below the late-August climatological mean of 23.7°C. Model consensus shows limited diurnal range with overnight lows near 10–13°C, positioning 21°C as the modal outcome while allowing modest upside risk to 22°C if clearing accelerates. Trader-implied probabilities reflect this narrow envelope of uncertainty ahead of final observational data.

Following the mid-August heatwave that delivered 38.1 °C at Kew Gardens, a cooler north-westerly flow and increasing cloud cover have reduced the risk of renewed warming. Typical August climatology centers on 22 °C, but model spread in boundary-layer mixing and any late-day showers introduces enough uncertainty to keep 20 °C and 23 °C live at combined 17 %. Official observations from London Heathrow or St James’s Park will resolve the market once the daily maximum is confirmed.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Northeast winds and post-frontal cooling are anchoring NYC’s highest temperature near the upper 70s on August 21, 2026.** Official National Weather Service forecasts call for a high of 79–81°F under partly sunny skies with a slight morning shower chance (20% or less), as a cool maritime air mass arrives from the northeast behind recent showers. Morning readings started in the low-to-mid 60s, limiting daytime rebound despite seasonal norms near 82–83°F. 

Model consensus and surface observations show modest heating under broken cloud cover and gusty northeast flow (10–15 mph with higher gusts), keeping the most probable range at 78–79°F (47% market-implied probability). Slightly warmer 80–81°F outcomes carry lower odds (14.5%) if afternoon sun breaks through more than expected, while cooler 76–77°F readings (24%) remain plausible if clouds thicken. No extreme heat or rapid warming signals appear in current guidance, consistent with traders pricing the narrow 76–81°F band as the dominant resolution zone.

Model consensus shows limited diurnal range with overnight lows near 10–13°C, positioning 21°C as the modal outcome while allowing modest upside risk to 22°C if clearing accelerates. Trader-implied probabilities reflect this narrow envelope of uncertainty ahead of final observational data.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble models favor maximum temperatures of 30–32°C in Tokyo on August 23 amid persistent summer conditions dominated by the subtropical high-pressure system. High humidity near 75–80% and the urban heat island effect elevate apparent temperatures, while scattered showers or weak frontal influences could cap peaks near the lower end of that range. Historical climatology shows late-August daily highs averaging 31°C, with recent seasonal outlooks indicating above-normal warmth across eastern Japan. Traders therefore cluster implied probabilities on 30°C and 31°C, reflecting uncertainty in the precise timing and intensity of any cloud cover or precipitation in the final 48-hour forecast window.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble forecasts indicate Tokyo will experience typical late-August conditions on the 23rd, with daytime maxima centered near 31–32 °C under the influence of the Pacific high and urban heat-island amplification. Higher outcomes above 33 °C would require clearer skies and stronger insolation, while lower readings hinge on earlier or heavier rainfall. This narrow scientific uncertainty, updated with the latest model runs, underpins the closely matched market-implied odds.
